title: Strict quotient and Roos reindexing before localization
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and g:X→Y a scheme isomorphism with l invertible in every residue field. Fix signed Roos shift comparisons at X and Y satisfying both coordinate laws. There are simultaneous strict-tower Roos and restricted-system comparisons. The Roos comparison is natural, its first and second coordinates equal the product comparison, and it commutes with the fixed signed shifts. The restricted-system comparison is the actual pullback-unit map on every section and every quotient level. These assertions concern arbitrary unbounded strict towers, without completeness. [def-pod-completion-reindex-models]

source.place: Steps 1 and 5; strict quotient and Roos comparison argument.

proof.text: Use the canonical scalarRoosMap. The additive-equivalence theorem makes it invertible, its defining coordinate theorem gives the first and second coordinate laws, and the naturality theorem gives naturality on all strict towers. The signed-shift compatibility theorem gives its remaining Roos law for the fixed signed shifts. Separately apply the actual inverse-image unit on coherent systems, mapped degreewise and transposed to a tower of complexes, to obtain the restricted-tower comparison with its section formula. Assemble those two isomorphism families. Good representatives are preserved by the identity-coefficient specialization of the existing K-flat model theorem.
